title: Flight booking service and its ports
name: Flight booking orchestration

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how BookingService uses the SeatInventory and PaymentGateway interfaces and handles their failures? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The seat commit fails with CommitFailure.HoldExpired after the customer has been charged. What happens in BookingService.book?
choices: The charge is kept and the caller receives a Booking, since payment is the source of truth
The booking is retried with a fresh hold before anything is reported
The charge is refunded (or flagged for manual review if the refund fails), the hold is released, and the caller receives BookingError.HoldExpired
The caller receives BookingError.HoldExpired and the charge stays in place until the reference is reused

questions.prompt: inventory.release(hold) is called on every failure path after a hold was taken, including when the hold has already expired. Which interface property makes that safe?
choices: hold() returns an Either, so release can only be reached with a valid hold
The SeatHold case class is immutable, so releasing it twice has no effect
release is declared to return Unit, and Scala ignores exceptions from Unit methods
The contract on release says it is safe for holds that were committed, expired or never existed

questions.prompt: A new case object HoldFailure.RegionClosed is added to the sealed trait, and no other file changes. What is the effect on BookingService?
choices: fromHold now has a non-exhaustive match, which the compiler reports as a warning (an error with fatal warnings), instead of failing at runtime
The code compiles silently and RegionClosed is mapped to TryAgain by the last case
The code compiles, and a MatchError is thrown the first time RegionClosed occurs, with no compiler diagnostic
The new case is ignored by the sealed trait until it is registered in the companion object
